# Caption notes (generated by ch3_figures_corrected.R; numbers computed from figdata_corrected/)

## Figure 1 (optimal policy)
- (a) μ first reaches 1.0 in 2119 (DICE 2023), 2125 (DICE-C), 2119 (DICE-CP). The GAMS μ ceiling binds in 2030–34 (0.24) for all three, and in 2035–39 (0.36) for DICE-CP only; it rises to 1.1 in 2120, allowing net-negative industrial CO₂.
- (b) The short savings spike around 2120 coincides with the μ ceiling rising from 1.0 to 1.1 (inherited GAMS schedule; anticipation is observed, not derived). From 2205 (outside this window) s is fixed at 0.28, as in GAMS.
- (c) Cumulative industrial CO₂ 2020–2100: DICE 2023 760 GtC, DICE-C 777 GtC, DICE-CP 738 GtC.

## Figure 2 (warming)
- (a) DICE-C first reaches 0.5 °C in 2291 and stays there from 2301: this is the lower bound on temperature inherited from the GAMS code (TATM.lo = 0.5, imposed by Nordhaus for numerical stability), not a physical result.
- (b) Colours as in (a); no separate legend.

## Figure 4 (atmospheric carbon)
- Peaks: DICE 2023 1,280 GtC in 2110; DICE-C 1,267 GtC in 2110; DICE-CP 1,310 GtC in 2108.
- DICE-C and DICE-CP start from the 2020 state of a historical spin-up of the Lenton carbon cycle (419 ppm), so there is no initial transient; DICE 2023 starts from its own 2020 DFAIR state.

## Figure 3 (permafrost carbon, DICE-CP)
- Both lines are DICE-CP. The GAMS-policy line is the same model run with the GAMS DICE 2023 controls (the Chapter 2 runs).
- (a) Frozen carbon lost by 2100: 209 GtC (GAMS policy) vs 215 GtC (re-optimized); by 2300: 93 vs 105 GtC.
- (b) Thawed pool peaks: 256.3 GtC in 2090 (GAMS DICE 2023 policy); 260.7 GtC in 2091 (Re-optimized policy).

## Figure 5 (welfare differences)
- ΔU_acc relative to the optimized DICE 2023 run (model units; no scale_2 constant). Solid = re-optimized policy, dot-dash = GAMS DICE 2023 policy (the Chapter 2 runs: the same models driven by the GAMS controls).
- U_acc(2300): DICE 2023 12052.0; DICE-C 12058.2 re-optimized / 12056.6 GAMS policy; DICE-CP 12046.1 / 12045.5.
- ΔU_acc(2300) from DICE 2023: DICE-C +6.2 / +4.5; DICE-CP -6.0 / -6.6 (re-optimized / GAMS policy).
- Gain from re-optimizing: DICE-C +1.6 (+0.014%), DICE-CP +0.6 (+0.005%).

## Figure 6 (DICE-CP temperature, GAMS policy vs re-optimized)
- Re-optimizing changes DICE-CP peak warming from 2.74 °C (2112) to 2.83 °C (2115), +0.10 °C; in 2300 from 0.42 to 0.55 °C (+0.13 °C).
- Both lines use the same model; the difference is due to the policy alone.

## Figure 6, five configurations (temperature)
- DICE 2023 is shown at its own optimum (solid). DICE-C and DICE-CP: dot-dash = GAMS DICE 2023 policy (Chapter 3 models driven by the GAMS controls), solid = re-optimized.
- Peaks: DICE 2023, Re-optimized policy: 2.76 °C (2117); DICE-C, GAMS DICE 2023 policy: 2.56 °C (2108); DICE-C, Re-optimized policy: 2.73 °C (2116); DICE-CP, GAMS DICE 2023 policy: 2.74 °C (2112); DICE-CP, Re-optimized policy: 2.83 °C (2115).
- DICE-CP's GAMS-policy peak is flat to ±0.0001 °C over 2124–2125.

## Figure A1 (time-step resolution)
- The annual grid (1 substep per year) is numerically unstable for the corrected surface ocean; solutions at 2 and 5 substeps per year coincide, and results are reported at 5.

## Figure A2 (DICE-CP multiple starts)
- (a) At the reporting resolution every start that converged reaches the same optimum.
- (b) On the annual grid, the cold start (GAMS controls) ends in a worse local optimum: μ collapses to near zero around Inf–-Inf.
- U_acc(2300) by run:

| Substeps/yr | Start | U_acc(2300) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | warm start from the 2-substep solution | 12046.1 |
| 2 | previous-optimum start | 12046.1 |
| 2 | GAMS-controls start | 12046.1 |

- A third 2-substep start (conservative) did not converge and is not shown.
